paragraphs.title: The Holy Garments and the Ephod

easy.question: Why were the holy garments made?
answers: To serve in the holy place
easy.explanation: The verse says the garments were made “to do service in the holy place.”

easy.question: For whom were the special holy garments made?
easy.explanation: The verse says they were the holy garments for Aaron.

easy.question: Which material is not mentioned among the ephod’s materials?
easy.explanation: Gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen are mentioned, but not wood.

medium.question: What did they do to the gold before weaving it into the threads?
answers: They beat it into thin plates
They sewed it to the shoulderpieces
medium.explanation: They first beat the gold into thin plates and then cut it into wires.

medium.question: In the phrase “fine twined linen,” what does “twined” describe?
medium.explanation: The phrase describes linen made from threads twisted or woven together.

medium.question: What does the repeated phrase “as the Lord commanded Moses” show?
answers: The garments were made according to precise instructions
The garments were made without planning
The garments were only for ordinary people
medium.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the work followed the instructions given to Moses.

challenge.question: How were the ephod’s shoulderpieces attached?
answers: They were joined at its two edges
They were joined only at the front
They were not attached to the ephod
challenge.explanation: The verse says they were coupled together by the two edges.

challenge.question: What was the main similarity between the ephod and its girdle?
answers: Both used the same materials and skilled workmanship
challenge.explanation: The girdle was made of the same materials and according to the same workmanship as the ephod.

challenge.question: What order of actions concerning the gold is described?
answers: They cut it into wires, embroidered it, and then beat it
They attached it to the shoulderpieces, dyed it, and then cut it
They beat it into plates, cut it into wires, and worked it into the threads
challenge.explanation: The verse describes beating the gold into plates, cutting it into wires, and working it into the colored threads and linen.

questions.question: How were the ephod’s shoulderpieces attached?
answers: They were joined at its two edges
They were joined only at the front
They were not attached to the ephod
questions.explanation: The verse says they were coupled together by the two edges.

questions.question: What was the main similarity between the ephod and its girdle?
answers: Both used the same materials and skilled workmanship
questions.explanation: The girdle was made of the same materials and according to the same workmanship as the ephod.

questions.question: What order of actions concerning the gold is described?
answers: They cut it into wires, embroidered it, and then beat it
They attached it to the shoulderpieces, dyed it, and then cut it
They beat it into plates, cut it into wires, and worked it into the threads
questions.explanation: The verse describes beating the gold into plates, cutting it into wires, and working it into the colored threads and linen.

paragraphs.title: The Onyx Stones on the Ephod’s Shoulders

easy.question: What kind of stones did they make?
easy.explanation: The verse says they made onyx stones.

easy.question: What was engraved on the stones?
easy.explanation: The names of the children of Israel were engraved on the stones.

easy.question: Where did they place the stones?
easy.explanation: The stones were placed on the shoulders of the ephod.

medium.question: What was the relationship between the names on the stones and the Israelites?
answers: They were the names of enemies
They were names of tabernacle vessels
medium.explanation: The stones bore the names of the Israelites and therefore represented them.

medium.question: In the phrase “inclosed in ouches of gold,” what does “ouches” mean?
answers: Set in or surrounded by gold frames
medium.explanation: The phrase describes stones held in gold settings or frames.

medium.question: Why were the stones memorial stones?
answers: Because they were found near a grave
Because they represented and recalled the Israelites
medium.explanation: They bore the names of the Israelites and served as a memorial for them.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the Israelites’ names being carried on the ephod’s shoulders?
answers: The priest carried their memorial before the Lord
The Israelites carried the ephod themselves
challenge.explanation: The stones were memorial stones placed on the shoulders, symbolizing the carrying of Israel’s remembrance.

challenge.question: What does “them” refer to in “he put them on the shoulders”?
challenge.explanation: “Them” refers to the onyx stones mentioned previously.

challenge.question: What does “as the Lord commanded Moses” emphasize?
answers: The stones were made without instructions
The work was done according to the Lord’s command
challenge.explanation: The closing phrase emphasizes obedience to the Lord’s instructions.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the Israelites’ names being carried on the ephod’s shoulders?
answers: The priest carried their memorial before the Lord
The Israelites carried the ephod themselves
questions.explanation: The stones were memorial stones placed on the shoulders, symbolizing the carrying of Israel’s remembrance.

questions.question: What does “them” refer to in “he put them on the shoulders”?
questions.explanation: “Them” refers to the onyx stones mentioned previously.

questions.question: What does “as the Lord commanded Moses” emphasize?
answers: The stones were made without instructions
The work was done according to the Lord’s command
questions.explanation: The closing phrase emphasizes obedience to the Lord’s instructions.

paragraphs.title: Making the Breastplate and Its Stones

easy.question: What materials were used to make the breastplate?
easy.explanation: The breastplate was made of gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen.

easy.question: What shape was the breastplate?
easy.explanation: It was foursquare and made double.

easy.question: How many rows of stones were on the breastplate?
easy.explanation: The passage describes four rows of stones.

medium.question: How were the twelve stones arranged?
answers: Four rows, with three stones in each row
Three rows, with four stones in each row
Two rows, with six stones in each row
medium.explanation: There were four rows, and each listed row contains three stones.

medium.question: Which group belonged to the second row?
answers: A sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle
An emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond
A beryl, an onyx, and a jasper
medium.explanation: The second row consisted of an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond.

medium.question: What are “ouches” in the phrase “inclosed in ouches of gold”?
medium.explanation: In this context, ouches are gold frames or settings holding the stones.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the names of the Israelites being on the stones?
answers: Each stone represented a tribe of Israel
challenge.explanation: The twelve stones corresponded to the names of the twelve tribes.

challenge.question: What does “every one with his name” emphasize?
answers: All the names were written together without distinction
Each stone had the separate name of one tribe
Only one name was engraved on the breastplate
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that each stone bore its own individual tribal name.

challenge.question: What does “like the engravings of a signet” indicate?
answers: The names were painted with removable color
The names were written on separate cloth
The names were engraved in the stones like a seal
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes permanent engraving, like letters cut into a seal.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the names of the Israelites being on the stones?
answers: Each stone represented a tribe of Israel
questions.explanation: The twelve stones corresponded to the names of the twelve tribes.

questions.question: What does “every one with his name” emphasize?
answers: All the names were written together without distinction
Each stone had the separate name of one tribe
Only one name was engraved on the breastplate
questions.explanation: The phrase shows that each stone bore its own individual tribal name.

questions.question: What does “like the engravings of a signet” indicate?
answers: The names were painted with removable color
The names were written on separate cloth
The names were engraved in the stones like a seal
questions.explanation: The phrase describes permanent engraving, like letters cut into a seal.

paragraphs.title: Attaching the Breastplate to the Ephod

easy.question: What were the chains on the breastplate made of?
easy.explanation: The chains were made of pure gold.

easy.question: How many gold rings were first placed on the ends of the breastplate?
easy.explanation: Two gold rings were placed on its two ends.

easy.question: What was used to attach the breastplate to the ephod?
easy.explanation: The breastplate was bound to the ephod with a lace of blue.

medium.question: What was the purpose of the chains and rings on the breastplate?
answers: To attach the breastplate to the ephod
medium.explanation: The chains passed through the rings and connected the breastplate to the ephod.

medium.question: Why was the breastplate bound to the ephod with blue thread?
answers: So it would not come loose from the ephod
medium.explanation: The verse says the binding kept the breastplate from being loosed from the ephod.

medium.question: What does “that it might be above the curious girdle” show?
answers: It was positioned above the ephod’s girdle
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the breastplate’s position above the ephod’s girdle.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the breastplate being attached at both upper and lower points?
answers: They intended to secure it firmly to the ephod
It consisted of two separate pieces
It was worn beneath the ephod
challenge.explanation: The different attachment points held it in place and prevented movement.

challenge.question: What order of actions is described?
answers: Binding the breastplate, making rings, and making chains
Making chains and rings, attaching them to the ephod, and tying the breastplate
Making the ephod, putting stones in the breastplate, and removing the rings
challenge.explanation: The chains and rings were made first, attached, and then the breastplate was secured with blue lace.

challenge.question: Which phrase identifies the breastplate’s position at the front of the ephod?
challenge.explanation: “Before it” indicates that the breastplate was placed at the front of the ephod.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the breastplate being attached at both upper and lower points?
answers: They intended to secure it firmly to the ephod
It consisted of two separate pieces
It was worn beneath the ephod
questions.explanation: The different attachment points held it in place and prevented movement.

questions.question: What order of actions is described?
answers: Binding the breastplate, making rings, and making chains
Making chains and rings, attaching them to the ephod, and tying the breastplate
Making the ephod, putting stones in the breastplate, and removing the rings
questions.explanation: The chains and rings were made first, attached, and then the breastplate was secured with blue lace.

questions.question: Which phrase identifies the breastplate’s position at the front of the ephod?
questions.explanation: “Before it” indicates that the breastplate was placed at the front of the ephod.

paragraphs.title: The Robe of the Ephod and the Pomegranates

easy.question: What was the ephod’s robe made of?
easy.explanation: The robe was made entirely of blue woven work.

easy.question: What was around the robe’s opening?
easy.explanation: The opening had a band around it so that it would not tear.

easy.question: What two things were placed around the robe’s hem?
easy.explanation: Pomegranates and gold bells were placed around the hem.

medium.question: Why was a band placed around the robe’s opening?
answers: So it would be strong and not tear
So it would be made of gold
So it would sound from far away
medium.explanation: The band was made so the robe would not tear.

medium.question: What does “a band round about the hole” mean?
medium.explanation: Here, “band” means a reinforced edge around the opening.

medium.question: What pattern appeared around the robe’s hem?
answers: A bell and a pomegranate in alternating order
Bells inside the robe without pomegranates
medium.explanation: The verse repeats the pattern: “A bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate.”

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the bells being placed “between the pomegranates”?
answers: The pomegranates were only painted designs
The bells were incorporated into the hem’s decoration
The bells hung above the robe
challenge.explanation: The bells were arranged among the pomegranate decorations around the hem.

challenge.question: What special feature of the robe is emphasized?
answers: It was plain blue with no decoration
It was woven and decorated with colors, pomegranates, and gold bells
challenge.explanation: The passage describes its weaving, colors, decorations, and bells.

challenge.question: What does “to minister” show about the robe?
answers: It was made according to the Lord’s command for holy service
It was only for beauty and display
challenge.explanation: The robe was made according to the command and for service in the holy place.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the bells being placed “between the pomegranates”?
answers: The pomegranates were only painted designs
The bells were incorporated into the hem’s decoration
The bells hung above the robe
questions.explanation: The bells were arranged among the pomegranate decorations around the hem.

questions.question: What special feature of the robe is emphasized?
answers: It was plain blue with no decoration
It was woven and decorated with colors, pomegranates, and gold bells
questions.explanation: The passage describes its weaving, colors, decorations, and bells.

questions.question: What does “to minister” show about the robe?
answers: It was made according to the Lord’s command for holy service
It was only for beauty and display
questions.explanation: The robe was made according to the command and for service in the holy place.

easy.question: For whom were the coats made?
easy.explanation: The coats were made for Aaron and his sons.

easy.question: Which item of clothing is mentioned in verse 28?
easy.explanation: The verse mentions linen breeches.

easy.question: Which colors are mentioned in verse 29?
easy.explanation: The verse names blue, purple, and scarlet.

medium.question: What was mentioned after the coats were made?
answers: The robe and the holy crown
medium.explanation: The passage next mentions the mitre and bonnets.

medium.question: What does “fine twined linen” describe?
medium.explanation: It describes linen made from threads twisted together.

medium.question: What does “as the Lord commanded Moses” emphasize?
answers: The garments were made by accident
The work followed the Lord’s command
medium.explanation: The phrase emphasizes obedience to the instructions given to Moses.

challenge.question: Which two items are described as being made of fine twined linen?
answers: The linen breeches and the girdle
challenge.explanation: The phrase is used for the linen breeches and the girdle.

challenge.question: What is distinctive about the girdle compared with the coats?
answers: It was made only for Aaron
It also included colored threads and needlework
challenge.explanation: The girdle included blue, purple, scarlet, and needlework.

challenge.question: Which item is correctly matched with its workmanship?
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically describes the girdle as made of needlework.

questions.question: Which two items are described as being made of fine twined linen?
answers: The linen breeches and the girdle
questions.explanation: The phrase is used for the linen breeches and the girdle.

questions.question: What is distinctive about the girdle compared with the coats?
answers: It was made only for Aaron
It also included colored threads and needlework
questions.explanation: The girdle included blue, purple, scarlet, and needlework.

questions.question: Which item is correctly matched with its workmanship?
questions.explanation: The verse specifically describes the girdle as made of needlework.

paragraphs.title: The Plate of the Holy Crown

easy.question: What was the plate of the holy crown made of?
easy.explanation: The verse says it was made of pure gold.

easy.question: What was written on the plate?
easy.explanation: The inscription was “Holiness To The Lord.”

easy.question: What did they make according to the beginning of the verse?
answers: The plate of the holy crown
easy.explanation: The verse begins by describing the making of the holy crown’s plate.

medium.question: Why was the plate associated with holiness?
answers: Because it said “Holiness To The Lord”
Because it was made of cloth
Because it was a musical instrument
medium.explanation: Its inscription declared that it was holy to the Lord.

medium.question: What was the “plate” in this context?
medium.explanation: It was a gold object bearing an engraved inscription.

medium.question: What did they do after making the plate of pure gold?
answers: They placed it in the ark
They wrote an inscription on it
medium.explanation: The passage says they wrote an inscription upon it.

challenge.question: What does “like to the engravings of a signet” mean?
answers: An inscription engraved like letters on a seal
A picture of a seal only
challenge.explanation: The words describe an inscription engraved in the manner of a seal.

challenge.question: What is the main idea of “Holiness To The Lord”?
answers: The plate belonged only to the people
The plate was dedicated to the Lord
challenge.explanation: The inscription declares that the plate was holy and dedicated to the Lord.

challenge.question: Which statement correctly combines the verse’s details?
answers: The plate was silver and used ordinarily
The plate was cloth with a picture on it
The plate was pure gold and engraved as holy to the Lord
challenge.explanation: The verse identifies both its material and its sacred inscription.

questions.question: What does “like to the engravings of a signet” mean?
answers: An inscription engraved like letters on a seal
A picture of a seal only
questions.explanation: The words describe an inscription engraved in the manner of a seal.

questions.question: What is the main idea of “Holiness To The Lord”?
answers: The plate belonged only to the people
The plate was dedicated to the Lord
questions.explanation: The inscription declares that the plate was holy and dedicated to the Lord.

questions.question: Which statement correctly combines the verse’s details?
answers: The plate was silver and used ordinarily
The plate was cloth with a picture on it
The plate was pure gold and engraved as holy to the Lord
questions.explanation: The verse identifies both its material and its sacred inscription.

paragraphs.title: The Blue Lace on the Mitre

easy.question: What did they put on the mitre?
easy.explanation: The verse says they tied a lace of blue to it.

easy.question: Where was the lace to be placed?
easy.explanation: It was fastened on the mitre.

easy.question: Whose command was being followed?
easy.explanation: The verse says it was done as the Lord commanded Moses.

medium.question: What does “as the Lord commanded” show?
answers: They did not know the command
medium.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the lace was placed according to the instructions.

medium.question: What does “on high upon the mitre” indicate?
answers: On the upper part of the mitre
medium.explanation: The phrase places the lace high on the mitre.

medium.question: What order of actions is described?
answers: They made a blue lace to fasten on the mitre
They put on the mitre and then removed the lace
They commanded Moses and then built the tabernacle
medium.explanation: The verse describes making the lace and fastening it on the mitre.

challenge.question: Where exactly was the lace placed?
challenge.explanation: The phrase “on high upon the mitre” places it above the mitre.

challenge.question: What was Moses’s relationship to the action?
answers: The work followed the command given to Moses
challenge.explanation: The verse says the Lord commanded Moses; Moses was not the one commanding the Lord.

challenge.question: What feature of the lace is emphasized?
challenge.explanation: The verse calls it a lace of blue.

questions.question: Where exactly was the lace placed?
questions.explanation: The phrase “on high upon the mitre” places it above the mitre.

questions.question: What was Moses’s relationship to the action?
answers: The work followed the command given to Moses
questions.explanation: The verse says the Lord commanded Moses; Moses was not the one commanding the Lord.

questions.question: What feature of the lace is emphasized?
questions.explanation: The verse calls it a lace of blue.

easy.question: What was completed?
answers: All the work of the tabernacle
easy.explanation: The verse says all the work of the tabernacle was finished.

easy.question: Who did all that the Lord commanded Moses?
easy.explanation: The verse specifically says the children of Israel did it.

easy.question: Who commanded Moses concerning the tabernacle?
easy.explanation: The verse says the Lord commanded Moses.

medium.question: What does “finished” mean in “all the work ... was finished”?
medium.explanation: The word indicates that all the tabernacle work had reached completion.

medium.question: What can be learned from the Israelites doing “all that the Lord commanded”?
answers: They did not finish the work
medium.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that they followed all the instructions.

medium.question: What does the verse mention after saying the work was finished?
answers: The Israelites doing all they had been commanded
medium.explanation: It says that the Israelites did according to everything commanded.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by the repeated idea “according to all ... so did they”?
answers: The work was only partly done
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes complete obedience to the divine command.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “the Lord commanded Moses”?
answers: The Lord gave Moses the instructions, and the Israelites carried them out
challenge.explanation: Moses received the instructions, and the Israelites acted according to them.

challenge.question: What is the grammatical difference between “was finished” and “the children of Israel did”?
answers: Both refer to exactly the same subject
The first refers to Moses and the second to the Lord
The first refers to the tabernacle work, and the second to the Israelites
challenge.explanation: The first describes completion of the work; the second describes the Israelites’ action.

questions.question: What is emphasized by the repeated idea “according to all ... so did they”?
answers: The work was only partly done
questions.explanation: The repetition emphasizes complete obedience to the divine command.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “the Lord commanded Moses”?
answers: The Lord gave Moses the instructions, and the Israelites carried them out
questions.explanation: Moses received the instructions, and the Israelites acted according to them.

questions.question: What is the grammatical difference between “was finished” and “the children of Israel did”?
answers: Both refer to exactly the same subject
The first refers to Moses and the second to the Lord
The first refers to the tabernacle work, and the second to the Israelites
questions.explanation: The first describes completion of the work; the second describes the Israelites’ action.

paragraphs.title: Bringing the Tabernacle and Its Coverings

easy.question: To whom did they bring the tabernacle?
easy.explanation: They brought the tabernacle to Moses.

easy.question: What did they bring with the tabernacle?
answers: The tent and all its furniture
easy.explanation: They brought the tent and all its furnishings, including its boards, bars, pillars, and sockets.

easy.question: Which coverings are mentioned?
answers: Rams’ skins dyed red and badgers’ skins
easy.explanation: The passage mentions red-dyed rams’ skins and badgers’ skins.

medium.question: What is described first?
answers: Bringing the tabernacle, tent, and furnishings
medium.explanation: The passage first describes bringing the tabernacle and its parts, then the coverings and veil.

medium.question: What does “covering” mean in this context?
medium.explanation: The skins served as coverings for the tabernacle.

medium.question: What can be understood from the detailed list of tabernacle parts?
answers: The tabernacle was not yet built
Only a small part was brought
It was brought with many organized components
medium.explanation: The listed hooks, boards, bars, pillars, and sockets show that a complete set of parts was brought.

challenge.question: What distinguishes the two coverings?
answers: One was made of red-dyed rams’ skins and the other of badgers’ skins
One was wood and the other metal
One was a veil and the other boards
challenge.explanation: The verse distinguishes the red-dyed rams’ skin covering from the badgers’ skin covering.

challenge.question: What does “the vail of the covering” indicate?
answers: The veil was used as a carrying tool
The veil served as a screen or partition
The veil was made of skins
challenge.explanation: A veil functions as a covering, screen, or divider.

challenge.question: What order is described?
answers: First the veil, then the boards, and finally the tent
First the badgers’ skins, then the pillars, and finally the hooks
First the tabernacle and its furnishings, then the coverings, and finally the veil
challenge.explanation: The passage begins with the tabernacle and its furnishings, continues with the coverings, and ends with the veil.

questions.question: What distinguishes the two coverings?
answers: One was made of red-dyed rams’ skins and the other of badgers’ skins
One was wood and the other metal
One was a veil and the other boards
questions.explanation: The verse distinguishes the red-dyed rams’ skin covering from the badgers’ skin covering.

questions.question: What does “the vail of the covering” indicate?
answers: The veil was used as a carrying tool
The veil served as a screen or partition
The veil was made of skins
questions.explanation: A veil functions as a covering, screen, or divider.

questions.question: What order is described?
answers: First the veil, then the boards, and finally the tent
First the badgers’ skins, then the pillars, and finally the hooks
First the tabernacle and its furnishings, then the coverings, and finally the veil
questions.explanation: The passage begins with the tabernacle and its furnishings, continues with the coverings, and ends with the veil.

paragraphs.title: The Holy Vessels Inside the Tabernacle

easy.question: What belonged with the ark of the testimony?
answers: Its staves and the mercy seat
easy.explanation: The passage lists the ark, its staves, and the mercy seat.

easy.question: What was placed on the table?
easy.explanation: The table is mentioned together with the shewbread.

easy.question: What was the oil for light used for?
easy.explanation: The oil for light was associated with the candlestick and its lamps.

medium.question: In what order are the first three main vessels listed?
medium.explanation: The passage lists the ark, then the table, and then the candlestick.

medium.question: What was the brass grate associated with?
medium.explanation: The grate belonged to the brasen altar.

medium.question: Which item is mentioned with the sweet incense?
medium.explanation: The golden altar and the sweet incense are listed together.

challenge.question: What did the ark and the brasen altar have in common?
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions staves for both the ark and the brasen altar.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the names “golden altar” and “brasen altar”?
answers: Both altars were made of gold
Both altars served exactly the same purpose
challenge.explanation: Their names identify different materials: gold and brass.

challenge.question: Which item appears after the candlestick and before the brasen altar?
challenge.explanation: The golden altar is listed after the candlestick and before the brasen altar.

questions.question: What did the ark and the brasen altar have in common?
questions.explanation: The passage mentions staves for both the ark and the brasen altar.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the names “golden altar” and “brasen altar”?
answers: Both altars were made of gold
Both altars served exactly the same purpose
questions.explanation: Their names identify different materials: gold and brass.

questions.question: Which item appears after the candlestick and before the brasen altar?
questions.explanation: The golden altar is listed after the candlestick and before the brasen altar.

paragraphs.title: The Tabernacle Court and Priestly Garments

easy.question: What is described in verse 40?
answers: The parts of the court and its service vessels
easy.explanation: The verse lists the court hangings, pillars, sockets, cords, pins, and service vessels.

easy.question: For whom were the holy garments in verse 41?
easy.explanation: The verse names Aaron the priest and his sons.

easy.question: What were Aaron’s sons’ garments for?
easy.explanation: Their garments were for ministering in the priestly office.

medium.question: What is the order of topics in verses 40–41?
answers: First the court and its vessels, then the priests’ garments
First the priests’ garments, then Israel’s journeys
First the offerings, then the altar

medium.question: What does “to minister in the priest’s office” mean?

medium.question: What distinction is made between the service garments and the holy garments?

The service garments were only for the people, while the holy garments were only for Moses
The service garments were for travel, while the holy garments were for building the court
medium.explanation: The verse first mentions garments for service and then specifically identifies garments for Aaron and his sons.

challenge.question: What conclusion follows from both verses together?

The tabernacle was only a residence for priests
The court was more important than holy service

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the court entrance was defined and organized?

The hanging for the court gate
The mention of the service garments
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically mentions the hanging for the court gate.

challenge.question: What is easy to overlook when comparing the verses?

Aaron’s sons were unrelated to holy service
The passage distinguishes general service garments from those specifically assigned to Aaron and his sons

The tabernacle was only a residence for priests
The court was more important than holy service

questions.question: Which detail shows that the court entrance was defined and organized?
answers: The mention of Aaron’s sons’ garments
The hanging for the court gate
The mention of the service garments

questions.question: What is easy to overlook when comparing the verses?
answers: The cords and pins belonged to the priests’ garments
Aaron’s sons were unrelated to holy service
The passage distinguishes general service garments from those specifically assigned to Aaron and his sons
questions.explanation: The passage first mentions service garments generally and then identifies the garments for Aaron and his sons.

easy.question: Who blessed the children of Israel?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Moses blessed them.

easy.question: Who did all the work?
easy.explanation: The passage says the children of Israel made all the work.

easy.question: What did Moses see?
easy.explanation: Moses looked upon all the work.

medium.question: What was the order of events?
answers: Command, the Israelites’ work, inspection, and blessing
medium.explanation: The Lord commanded, the Israelites worked, Moses inspected the work, and then blessed them.

medium.question: Why did Moses bless the Israelites?
answers: They asked him for a blessing
He saw that they had done as commanded
They had completed their wilderness journey
medium.explanation: Moses blessed them after seeing that they had followed the command.

medium.question: What does “all the work” mean in this context?
answers: The work and construction that had been done
medium.explanation: Moses inspected everything the Israelites had made.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the repeated idea “even so had they done it”?
answers: The Israelites carried out the command exactly
Moses did not know what they were told to do
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that their work matched the Lord’s command.

challenge.question: What does Moses seeing the work before blessing the Israelites show?
answers: The blessing came before the work began
The blessing followed inspection and approval of the work
Moses himself did all the work
challenge.explanation: The order shows that Moses inspected the completed work and then blessed them.

challenge.question: What important point is shared by both verses?
answers: The Israelites worked without a command
The work was done according to the Lord’s command
challenge.explanation: Both verses emphasize that the work followed the Lord’s instructions.
